title: Support Vector Machines — interaktiv verstehen
category_reason: Interactive teaching page on the SVM, a core ML classifier (max-margin, kernel trick, SMO training).
thesis: A library-free HTML/CSS/JS interactive explaining the SVM: the classifier that finds the widest-margin separating hyperplane, plus the kernel trick and a live SMO playground.
key_claims: The SVM picks the separating hyperplane farthest from both classes; margin = 2/||w||, so maximizing the margin is minimizing ||w||.
Only the support vectors determine the decision boundary; deleting every other point changes nothing.
Kernel trick: points need never be transformed explicitly — a kernel K(a,b) computes inner products in the high space directly (RBF exp(-gamma*||a-b||^2), poly (a^T b + 1)^d).
Soft margin: slack variables xi_i allow violations, and C controls how expensive they are; large C -> overfitting risk, small C -> smoother boundary tolerating outliers.
Optimization problem: min 1/2||w||^2 + C*sum xi_i subject to y_i(w^T x_i + b) >= 1 - xi_i, xi_i >= 0.
A simplified SMO (Sequential Minimal Optimization) is implemented to train live and redraw the decision-region heatmap.
visualizations: canvas 2D margin demo: draggable separating line (angle/offset), margin corridor, animated 'find optimum' search
canvas pseudo-3D 'kernel lift' (z = x^2+y^2) morph showing a flat plane separates rings in 3D
canvas live playground: click to add +1/-1 points, SMO retrain, bilinear-smoothed decision heatmap, margin contours, linear/RBF/poly tabs and C/gamma sliders
internal_tensions: Claims 'no framework, no libraries' yet ships a hand-rolled numerical SMO that may not fully converge (maxPass=12, tol=1e-3).
The 3D 'a flat plane separates the rings' is an illustrative analogy, not the literal linear SVM in that lifted space.

title: McCulloch & Pitts (1943) – Interaktiv Erleben
category_reason: Interactive walkthrough of the 1943 paper that founded artificial neural networks and their computational equivalence to Turing machines.
thesis: An interactive retelling of McCulloch & Pitts (1943): neurons are all-or-none logical switches, their networks realize AND/OR/NOT and are computationally equivalent to Turing machines — the 'birth certificate of AI'.
key_claims: A neuron fires all-or-none like a bit (0/1); a threshold determines when it fires.
Neuron networks realize the logic gates AND (threshold 2), OR (threshold 1) and NOT (via inhibition).
Every logical function/expression can be built as a neuron network (their Theorem 2).
Inhibition has absolute veto: a single inhibitory synapse blocks firing no matter how many excitatory inputs arrive.
Circular/recurrent nets let activity circulate -> memory and reference to past events; variable synapses can be replaced by loops (Theorem 7), so learning ~ recurrent activity.
A network plus a memory/tape computes exactly what a Turing machine can, and vice versa.
visualizations: DOM neuron threshold demo (stimulus vs threshold sliders, fire/silence)
DOM logic-gate toggles (AND/OR/AND-NOT with truth outputs)
canvas neuron-network animation of the paper's 'heat after a short cold stimulus' example (delay + AND + inhibition)
DOM time-step 'circuit' loop for memory (start/stop/inhibit to wipe it)
DOM memory-matching game pairing concepts + SVG progress ring
internal_tensions: The 'Turing equivalence' and 'every program buildable' claims are presented pedagogically, not as a formal proof.
Conflates 'learning' with recurrence/loops (a loose reading of their Theorem 7).

Points begin scattered and 'cascade'/collapse onto the target manifold once the network discovers that structure.

title: Q·K → Simplex, V → Meaning Flow — How Attention Builds Simplicial Complexes
category_reason: Applies simplicial-complex / topological-data-analysis ideas to transformer self-attention (edges/triangles from attention, Betti numbers).
thesis: A Plotly interactive showing how attention builds a simplicial complex: Q·K attention scores above a threshold create 1-simplices (edges) and mutually attending triples create 2-simplices (triangles), through which V vectors carry 'meaning'; Betti numbers are reported.
key_claims: Words are 0-simplices: embeddings in a 3D semantic space whose axes are Male/Female, Animal/Divine, Weak/Strong (from a fixed toy lexicon).
An edge {i,j} exists iff min(alpha_ij, alpha_ji) > epsilon; a triangle exists iff all three mutual attention weights exceed epsilon.
Q = X·W_Q ('what am I looking for'), K = X·W_K ('what do I offer'), V = X·W_V (content that flows); scores = Q·K^T/sqrt(d), softmax -> attention; output = weighted sum of V.
Betti numbers are computed via union-find: beta_0 = connected components, beta_1 = loops (edges - (n - components) - triangles).
W_Q, W_K, W_V are user-editable 3x3 matrices; threshold epsilon and softmax sharpness are sliders.
methods_math: Betti numbers beta_0, beta_1 via union-find / loop counting
hash-based fallback embedding for out-of-lexicon words
visualizations: Plotly 3D scatter/mesh: embedding points, Q (diamond) and K (square) vectors, edges (lines), triangles (mesh3d), dotted Q->K lines, V-output (cross) markers; epsilon-threshold and sharpness sliders; editable W_Q/W_K/W_V matrix inputs; sentence text input; info panel listing vertices/edges/triangles + Betti numbers
internal_tensions: The semantic 3D space is a hand-authored toy lexicon (gender/being/power), not a real LLM embedding.
The beta_1 formula is a rough approximation (assumes triangles fill loops), not a true homology computation.
'V flows meaning along simplices' is a narrative metaphor, not the actual linear weighted-sum computation.

title: Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems — Interactive Explainer
category_reason: A pure math-logic explainer of Gödel's incompleteness theorems; AI is only mentioned in passing as a ripple effect.
thesis: An interactive tabbed explainer of Gödel's 1931 incompleteness theorems: Gödel numbering lets mathematics talk about itself, and a self-referential formula G ('G is not provable') is true yet unprovable — so no sufficiently strong, consistent, recursively-axiomatized system is complete, nor can it prove its own consistency.
key_claims: Gödel numbering encodes symbols/formulas/proofs as natural numbers via prime factorization, making 'provability' an arithmetic (recursive) property.
The formula R(q);q asserts its own unprovability — a liar-paradox made rigorous, true but unprovable inside the system.
First Incompleteness (Satz VI): every omega-consistent recursive class of formulas has undecidable formulas.
Second Incompleteness (Satz XI): a consistent system cannot prove its own consistency.
Theorem VII: every recursive relation is arithmetical; Theorem X: the first-order Entscheidungsproblem is undecidable.
This killed Hilbert's program and influenced Turing (halting), Church, Cohen (CH independent of ZFC); Penrose's 'mind transcends algorithms' is flagged as controversial.
visualizations: tabbed DOM interface (6 tabs)
interactive Gödel-number calculator (BigInt prime powers) + symbol grid
self-reference 'Reason About It' cycler and a depth-of-understanding slider (levels 0-4)
step-by-step proof reveal (Next/All/Reset, 9 steps)
system evaluator (consistent / powerful-enough / recursive checkboxes -> 'Gödel strikes')
internal_tensions: Uses the original (stronger) omega-consistency statement of the 1st theorem; modern versions use mere consistency (Rosser).
The Penrose/mind claims are presented as a controversial ripple, not endorsed.

title: Positional Encoding — Die Unendlichkeitsmaschine
category_reason: Explains the transformer's sinusoidal positional encoding (a core component of the attention/transformer architecture).
thesis: Positional encoding explained as an 'Unendlichkeitsmaschine' (infinity-machine) gear cascade: 7 frequency-dimensions each rotating exponentially slower than the last, together producing a unique interference pattern — the fingerprint of each position.
key_claims: Each gear = one frequency dimension of the sinusoidal positional encoding; the frequencies form a geometric progression (fast to slow).
The fastest gear distinguishes adjacent positions; the slowest needs ~10,000 positions for a full rotation (distinguishing text start from middle).
Each position's encoding is a unique interference pattern; neighboring positions give similar patterns (similar embeddings), far ones very different.
The sin/cos trick: cos(a-b)=cos a cos b + sin a sin b -> the similarity of two positions depends only on their distance, not absolute position (so the model can learn '3 tokens back').

title: Étale Raum & Étale Kohomologie — visuell
category_reason: Pure algebraic geometry / number theory (étale cohomology, Weil conjectures, ℓ-adic cohomology); no AI application.
thesis: A visual tour of étale space and étale cohomology: the étale space of a sheaf (stalks over the base), étale morphisms as algebraic (unbranched) coverings, the étale site (a Grothendieck topology), Čech cohomology (gluing on overlaps), and the payoff — ℓ-adic cohomology and Frobenius eigenvalues behind the Weil conjectures / Deligne's Riemann hypothesis over finite fields.
key_claims: The étale space Ét(F) is the disjoint union of stalks F_x; a section is a continuous section of the projection pi, which is a local homeomorphism (hence 'étale').
An étale morphism = flat + unbranched = a local-homeomorphism analogue that works in positive characteristic (e.g. z -> z^n on C*).
The étale site replaces open sets by étale morphisms with surjective étale families as covers — a Grothendieck topology that needs no points.
Čech cohomology measures how local sections fail to glue to global ones; the cocycle condition dc=0 (e.g. c_23 - c_13 + c_12 = 0 mod 4).
Étale cohomology gives finite-dimensional Q_l spaces with a Frobenius action; #X(F_{q^n}) = sum (-1)^i tr(Frob^n | H^i_et); Deligne showed |eigenvalue| = q^{i/2} (Riemann over finite fields).
Comparison theorem: for smooth X/C, H^i_et(X, Z/n) is isomorphic to the singular cohomology H^i(X(C), Z/n).
methods_math: Frobenius action / Weil conjectures / Lefschetz trace formula
visualizations: canvas étale space (base line X, vertical stalks, a section running on one sheet, sheet-count slider + 'wiggle section')
canvas covering z -> z^n (base circle, n preimages, monodromy rotation toggle, degree slider)
canvas étale site (add surjective étale 'covers' drawn as multi-sheet arcs over X)

canvas Frobenius eigenvalues (elliptic-curve-style spectrum, q=5; weight circles 1, sqrt(q), q; Frob^n slider -> Lefschetz sum)
MathJax-rendered formulas throughout
internal_tensions: Visual/metaphorical — 'étale site covers' drawn as arcs is an analogy; the real object is a category with a coverage notion.
The Frobenius widget is one specific toy (q=5, a single elliptic-curve-like spectrum), not a general computation.

thesis: An interactive overview of Hermann Schmitz's 'Philosophie des Leibes': Leib vs Körper (the felt, surfaceless body), the vital dynamic Enge <-> Weite, feelings as spatially poured atmospheres, bodily communication (Einleibung), personhood requiring the body, the ethics of the atomic bomb, and animal consciousness via 'Du-Evidenz'.

Personhood = the capacity for self-attribution, possible only through being affektively affected (bodily); the person lives between personal emancipation (reason) and personal regression (rapture).

The atomic bomb destroyed war's 'serious school' for integrating emancipation and regression, stranding humanity at too high an emancipation level, leaving unmet regression needs (traffic, sport, festivals).

title: Bruchkanten im Gedankenraum — ganz einfach erklärt
category_reason: Explains a 2025 result on the geometry of LLM token-embedding spaces (manifold hypothesis violation) — a question about ML models.
thesis: A no-math, plain-language version of Robinson, Dey & Chiang (2025, NeurIPS): token-embedding spaces of real LLMs are NOT smooth manifolds — they have 'Bruchkanten' (singularities / break-edges), which is why near-identical prompts can yield wildly different answers.
key_claims: Most AI work silently assumes model 'thoughts' lie on a smooth curved surface (manifold); this paper tests that and finds it false for real LLMs.
The test: zoom in at a point — if the neighborhood looks like a flat disc it is smooth, otherwise it is a singularity (Bruchkante).
Dimension trick: count neighbors in a ball — volume ~ K*r^d, so the log-log slope = dimension; a suddenly RISING slope signals a break-edge.
On 4 real models (~12 h compute each): 4/4 reject the manifold hypothesis; 3/4 also reject the milder fiber-bundle hypothesis; min p-value 3e-8 (GPT2); GPT2's dimension ranges 20-531 (not constant).
GPT2's dimension distribution has three peaks (~20 for numbers/months/days, ~389 single words, ~531 word-fragments); some words have dimension 0 (isolated points).

Prompts aren't portable: Llemma7B vs Mistral7B (same 32,016-token vocab) have very different geometry (median dim 4096 vs 48); longer context does not 'heal' singularities; singularities can reach the output.

Honesty corner: non-rejection is not evidence of smoothness; the test detects but does not classify the kind of break-edge; validity is limited to radii below the hard-to-estimate 'reach'; boundary points are missed (sensitivity vs specificity).
methods_math: local dimension estimation via volume scaling V(r)~K*r^d (log-log slope)
visualizations: canvas demo 1: two prompt answer-clouds — a 'Bruchkante' slider splits cloud B into clusters (prompt fragility)
canvas demo 2: zoom-test on a circle (smooth) vs a cusp (singularity) with position + zoom sliders and a 'flache Scheibe' vs 'Singularität' verdict
canvas demo 3: build a log-log volume curve with two slopes (left/right of a kink) — rising slope -> 'Bruchkante!' verdict
big-number stat cards (4/4, 3/4, 3e-8, 20-531)
internal_tensions: An explicit 'honesty corner' — a non-rejection is not evidence of smoothness, and the test neither classifies singularities nor is valid above the 'reach'.
The demo clouds/shapes are didactic rebuilds, not real model weights; all figures are quoted from the paper's tables/figures.
